text:
Alex Chen: Heads up — ScaleMate (pilot customer) just asked for prescriptive guidance + runtime flags for mobile-first batching + quantization. They want an alpha pilot next month. Can we scope what we can commit?
Maria Lopez: ScaleMate asks sound like: (1) small-batch low-latency mode, (2) int8 quant recs + safe fallbacks, (3) eval-triggered alerts when quality regresses.
Kevin O'Riley: For small-batch low-latency we need: adaptive batching with latency SLO, prefix caching, and a client-side hint to keep batching windows small. Also SDK flag so mobile apps can opt-in.
Jamal Singh: +1. Operational constraints: can we guarantee p95 latency under 200ms for 1-2 token responses? Need SRE input on CPU/GPU packing overhead at that case.
Sophia Park: From product POV pilot acceptance: p95 latency < 120ms for 1-2 token cases, end-to-end token-cost reduction >= 20% vs no-opt, and no quality regression (eval delta < 0.02 on our prompt set). If those hold, we can consider pilot a success.
Kevin O'Riley: Proposed runtime config to start with (rough):
```
optimize: {
  batching: {mode: "adaptive", max_latency_ms: 60, min_batch_size: 1, mobile_hint: true},
  cache: {prefix_kv: true, ttl_ms: 30000},
  quant: {preferred: "int8", fallback: "fp16", quality_guard: 0.02}
}
```
Alex Chen: That looks good. Question: do we expose the quant fallback as automatic (platform decides) or explicit (customer chooses)? ScaleMate wants auto to simplify integration.
Maria Lopez: Auto fallback is easier for customers but we should include an opt-out flag in SDK. Also telemetry must surface when fallback happens.
Jamal Singh: SRE-Bot — can you run quick capacity estimate for adaptive batching with these settings? Looking for expected GPU utilization delta and any queuing risk.
SRE-Bot: @Jamal Singh queued a capacity run: sim params (traffic: 10 rps/mobile, batch window: 60ms, model: redwood-v1-8b-int8). ETA 18h for simulation results.
Kevin O'Riley: Implementation notes: need a small SDK patch (iOS/Android) to set mobile_hint and expose a remote-config flag. Platform: add signal events for quant-fallback and eval-alert triggers.
Sophia Park: Launch gating checklist (alpha):
- SDK flags shipped (iOS + Android)
- Runtime support for mobile adaptive batching + prefix cache
- Quant recommendation engine with fallback telemetry
- Eval suite for ScaleMate prompt set + automated alerting on regressions
- Pilot dashboard for cost/latency/quality per-customer
Alex Chen: Timeline: can eng deliver a minimal alpha in 4 weeks? If not, negotiate push to 6 weeks with ScaleMate.
Kevin O'Riley: 4 weeks is tight but doable with a focused slice: runtime knobs + telemetry + SDK flag. Full quant recommendation engine needs longer (8-12w). We can ship a heuristic rule-set for alpha.
Maria Lopez: Customer comms: propose an alpha that requires a one-week integration window on their side and a 4-week pilot data collection. They accept a heuristic approach as long as we alert on fallback events.
Jamal Singh: Risks: quality regressions with int8 on some prompts. Mitigation: eval-triggered alerts and auto-fallback to fp16 on detected regressions; also a manual kill-switch for customer.
Sophia Park: Acceptance criteria re-stated for the alpha: p95 latency < 120ms (1-2 token paths), cost delta <= -20%, quality delta <= 0.02 OR automatic fallback observed and documented.
Alex Chen: OK. Action items: @Kevin implement runtime knobs + telemetry (owner), @Jamal run capacity sim and share numbers (owner), @Maria draft pilot comms and success criteria for ScaleMate (owner), @Sophia coordinate eval harness and dashboard (owner).
Maria Lopez: I’ll draft the pilot email today and include optional rollback steps.
Kevin O'Riley: Will start a branch for the runtime patch and add the SDK opt-in flag PR by EOD Wednesday.
Jamal Singh: SRE-Bot noted. I’ll follow up with simulation results and a short risk summary.
Alex Chen: Thanks all. If anyone sees scope creep, ping me. ScaleMate is enthusiastic but we need to be disciplined on alpha scope. :thumbsup:
